import Mathlib
import Catalog.Logic.ProofComplexity.SimulationPreorder
import Catalog.Logic.ProofComplexity.SimulationDegrees
import Catalog.Logic.ProofComplexity.DegreeLattice

/-! # Density along the whole height ladder of p-degrees

This file is a **fifth-cycle** companion to the order-type development.  `OrderType.lean`
exhibited a *single* density witness `interSys`, strictly between `linSystem` and
`fibSystem`.  `DegreeLattice.lean` built the infinite height ladder `powSystem k`
(size `2 ^ (n ^ k)`) with `powSystem k < powSystem (k+1)` for `k ≥ 1`.

Here we prove **density at every rung of the ladder simultaneously**: between any two
consecutive ladder degrees there is a strictly intermediate p-degree
(`exists_strictly_between_powSystem`).  The witness `interPowSys k` is the *parity-glued*
size function that runs the upper rate `2 ^ (n ^ (k+1))` on the even indices and the lower
rate `2 ^ (n ^ k)` on the odd indices: super-polynomially above the lower rung (the even
indices keep the faster rate), yet too thin to recover the upper rung (the odd indices fall
back to the slower rate).  This is a *local-to-global* glueing: a degree is assembled from
the two rates prescribed on the two residue classes mod 2.

The engine is the domination characterisation `simulates_sysOfSize_iff` together with the
uniform gap `pow_pow_succ_gap_strong`, an "all-large-`n`" strengthening of
`DegreeLattice.pow_pow_succ_gap` that lets us select a witness of prescribed parity.

-- !-- Lab Notebook -- !--
Hypothesis : The single Fibonacci-vs-linear density witness should generalise to *every*
             consecutive pair `powSystem k < powSystem (k+1)` on the height ladder, via the
             same parity-thinning trick applied to the ladder's exponents.
Result     : Confirmed, `sorry = 0`.  `interPowSys k` lies strictly between `powSystem k`
             and `powSystem (k+1)` for every `k ≥ 1` (`powSystem_lt_interPow`,
             `interPow_lt_powSystem_succ`, `exists_strictly_between_powSystem`).
Insight    : Whereas `DegreeLattice.pow_pow_succ_gap` only produced *one* exponent `n`
             realising the super-polynomial gap, density needs a gap witness of a *chosen
             parity*.  Strengthening to "the gap holds for **all** `n ≥ c + 2`"
             (`pow_pow_succ_gap_strong`) makes the parity free: pick an even or odd witness
             above the threshold as needed.  The clean bound is
             `(2^(n^k)+2)^c ≤ 2^(c·n^k + c) < 2^(n^(k+1))` whenever `n ≥ c + 2`, since then
             `c·n^k + c < n·n^k = n^(k+1)`.
Failure analysis : Reusing `pow_pow_succ_gap` verbatim fails because its witness `n = c + 2`
             has a fixed parity, so it can only refute *one* of the two simulations needed
             to sandwich `interPowSys`.  The all-large-`n` form removes that coupling.
-- !-- Lab Notebook -- !--
-/

set_option maxHeartbeats 1000000

namespace ProofComplexity

/-! ## A uniform (all-large-`n`) super-polynomial gap -/

/-
!-- comment: For `k ≥ 1` the rungs `2^(n^k)` and `2^(n^(k+1))` are super-polynomially
apart for *every* `n ≥ c + 2`, not just one — so a witness of either parity
is available. -- !--

**Uniform ladder gap.**  For `k ≥ 1` and every exponent `c`, the inequality
`(2 ^ (n ^ k) + 2) ^ c < 2 ^ (n ^ (k + 1))` holds for *all* `n ≥ c + 2`.
-/
lemma pow_pow_succ_gap_strong (k : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) (c : ℕ) :
    ∀ n, c + 2 ≤ n → (2 ^ (n ^ k) + 2) ^ c < 2 ^ (n ^ (k + 1)) := by
  -- Apply the power inequality: $(2^{n^k} + 2)^c \leq 2^{c \cdot (n^k + 1)}$
  have h_pow : ∀ n, c + 2 ≤ n → (2 ^ (n ^ k) + 2) ^ c ≤ 2 ^ (c * (n ^ k + 1)) := by
    intros n hn; rw [ pow_mul' ] ; gcongr;
    rw [ pow_succ' ] ; linarith [ Nat.pow_le_pow_right ( by decide : 1 ≤ 2 ) ( show n ^ k ≥ 1 by exact Nat.one_le_pow _ _ ( by linarith ) ) ];
  refine fun n hn ↦ lt_of_le_of_lt ( h_pow n hn ) ?_;
  gcongr <;> norm_num;
  rw [ pow_succ' ] ; nlinarith [ Nat.pow_le_pow_right ( by linarith : 1 ≤ n ) hk ] ;

/-! ## The parity-glued intermediate system -/

-- !-- comment: Upper rate `2^(n^(k+1))` on even indices, lower rate `2^(n^k)` on odd
--             indices: a degree glued from the two rates on the two residue classes. -- !--
/-- The parity-glued intermediate system: size `2 ^ (n ^ (k+1))` on even `n`, size
`2 ^ (n ^ k)` on odd `n`. -/
def interPowSys (k : ℕ) : ProofSystem.{0, 0} ℕ :=
  sysOfSize (fun n => if Even n then 2 ^ (n ^ (k + 1)) else 2 ^ (n ^ k))

/-! ## `powSystem k < interPowSys k` -/

/-
!-- comment: Lower rung simulates the glued system (its size is everywhere `≥ 2^(n^k)`),
but the glued system cannot be simulated by the lower rung because the even
indices keep the faster rate (uniform gap at an even witness). -- !--

The lower ladder rung is strictly below the glued system: `powSystem k < interPowSys k`
for `k ≥ 1`.
-/
theorem powSystem_lt_interPow (k : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) :
    powSystem k < interPowSys k := by
  constructor;
  · convert simulates_sysOfSize_iff _ _ |>.2 ⟨ id, polyMono_id, ?_ ⟩;
    intro n; split_ifs <;> simp_all +decide [ Nat.pow_succ ] ;
    rcases n with ( _ | _ | n ) <;> simp_all +decide [ Nat.pow_succ', Nat.pow_mul ];
    · cases k <;> norm_num at *;
    · exact Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero.mpr ( by positivity );
  · intro h;
    obtain ⟨ f, hf_mono, hf_bound ⟩ := simulates_sysOfSize_iff _ _ |>.1 h;
    obtain ⟨ c, hc ⟩ := hf_mono.2;
    have := pow_pow_succ_gap_strong k hk c ( 2 * ( c + 2 ) ) ( by linarith );
    grind

/-! ## `interPowSys k < powSystem (k+1)` -/

/-
!-- comment: The glued system simulates the upper rung (its size is everywhere
`≤ 2^(n^(k+1))`), but the upper rung cannot be simulated by the glued system
because the odd indices fall back to the slower rate (uniform gap at an odd
witness). -- !--

The glued system is strictly below the upper ladder rung: `interPowSys k < powSystem
(k+1)` for `k ≥ 1`.
-/
theorem interPow_lt_powSystem_succ (k : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) :
    interPowSys k < powSystem (k + 1) := by
  refine' lt_of_le_not_ge _ _;
  · refine' simulates_sysOfSize_iff _ _ |>.2 ⟨ _, polyMono_id, fun n => _ ⟩;
    split_ifs <;> [ exact le_rfl; exact pow_le_pow_right₀ ( by decide ) ( Nat.pow_le_pow_right ( Nat.pos_of_ne_zero ( by aesop ) ) ( by linarith ) ) ];
  · -- Suppose for contradiction that `powSystem (k+1) ≤ interPowSys k`.
    by_contra h_contra
    unfold powSystem interPowSys at h_contra;
    obtain ⟨ f, hf_mono, hf_bound ⟩ := simulates_sysOfSize_iff _ _ |>.1 h_contra;
    -- Choose an ODD witness `n := 2 * (c + 2) + 1`. Then `¬ Even n` (so the if-branch is `2^(n^k)`) and `c + 2 ≤ n`.
    obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ : ∃ c, ∀ m, f m + 1 ≤ (m + 2) ^ c := by
      exact hf_mono.2
    set n := 2 * (c + 2) + 1 with hn_def
    have hn_odd : ¬Even n := by
      grind
    have hn_ge : c + 2 ≤ n := by
      grind;
    have := pow_pow_succ_gap_strong k hk c n hn_ge;
    grind

/-! ## Density at every rung -/

-- !-- comment: Sandwiching the two strict steps: a strictly intermediate degree exists
--             between every pair of consecutive ladder rungs. -- !--
/-- **Density along the ladder.**  For every `k ≥ 1` there is a p-degree strictly between
the consecutive ladder rungs `powSystem k` and `powSystem (k+1)`. -/
theorem exists_strictly_between_powSystem (k : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) :
    ∃ S : ProofSystem.{0, 0} ℕ, powSystem k < S ∧ S < powSystem (k + 1) :=
  ⟨interPowSys k, powSystem_lt_interPow k hk, interPow_lt_powSystem_succ k hk⟩

end ProofComplexity

import Mathlib

/-!
# Tropical Gravitational Lensing for Integer Factorization

Domain: Pythagorean.

This file develops a precise mathematical core for the metaphor of **tropical
gravitational lensing applied to integer factorization**, tying together four
existing catalog directions:

* `Algebra/BerggrenLorentz/Core.lean` — Pythagorean triples and difference of squares;
* `Bridges/CategoricalTropicalUltrametric.lean` — tropical (min-plus) ↔ ultrametric;
* `Computation/PadicValuationDepth.lean` — p-adic valuation as a non-archimedean depth;
* `Geometry/StereographicSheaf.lean` — conformal / quadratic geometry of squares.

## The dictionary (metaphor → mathematics)

| Lensing notion            | Precise object                                            |
|---------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
| light ray                 | an integer / factor candidate                            |
| lensing mass              | a prime `p`                                               |
| deflection of a ray       | the `p`-adic valuation `v_p`                              |
| lens equation (mass adds) | `v_p (a*b) = v_p a + v_p b`  (tropicalization of `*`)     |
| caustic / strong focusing | ultrametric `min (v_p a) (v_p b) ≤ v_p (a+b)`             |
| image separation          | Fermat's `n = a² - b² = (a-b)(a+b)`                       |
| natural lens images       | Pythagorean triples `x²+y²=z² ⇒ x² = (z-y)(z+y)`          |

The conceptual punchline, made into theorems below: **factorization of `n` at a
prime `p` IS a tropical (additive) partition of the deflection `v_p n`**, and the
geometry that produces the factor pairs `(a-b, a+b)` is exactly the Pythagorean /
difference-of-squares geometry studied in the Berggren–Lorentz file.

## Main results

* `fermat_diff_sq`, `fermat_factor_dvd`, `composite_of_fermat` — difference of
  squares ↔ factorization ("image separation" gives a factor).
* `pythag_leg_factor` — every Pythagorean triple lenses a leg-square into two images.
* `trop_lens_mul` — the multiplicative lens equation (deflection adds).
* `trop_lens_caustic` — the ultrametric focusing inequality.
* `lens_metric_ultrametric` — the strong triangle inequality of the `p`-adic lens metric.
* `padicValNat_sq`, `pythag_lens_depth` — the lensed Pythagorean leg has *even* total
  deflection, tropically partitioned between the two images.
* `lens_depth_partition` — factorization = additive partition of valuation depth.
-/

namespace Pythagorean.TropicalLensingFactorization

/-! ## §1. Image separation: difference of squares = factorization

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
Hypothesis: Fermat's identity `n = a² - b² = (a-b)(a+b)` is the arithmetic analogue
of a gravitational lens producing two images `a-b` (close image) and `a+b` (far
image) of a single source `n`. We verify the algebra over `ℤ` (clean, no truncated
subtraction) and then extract a composite-detection criterion over `ℕ`.
-- !-- end -- !--
-/

/-
The Fermat "two-image" identity: a difference of squares splits into two factors.
-/
theorem fermat_diff_sq (a b : ℤ) : (a - b) * (a + b) = a ^ 2 - b ^ 2 := by
  grind

/-
"Close image" `a-b` always divides `n = a² - b²`: a lensed factor.
-/
theorem fermat_factor_dvd (n a b : ℤ) (h : n = a ^ 2 - b ^ 2) : (a - b) ∣ n := by
  exact h.symm ▸ ⟨ a + b, by ring ⟩

/-- A number with a nontrivial divisor `< n` is composite. -/
def IsComposite (n : ℕ) : Prop := ∃ d, d ∣ n ∧ 1 < d ∧ d < n

/-
Difference-of-squares form of `Nat.sq_sub_sq`, oriented as a product of images.
-/
theorem fermat_identity (a b : ℕ) : (a - b) * (a + b) = a ^ 2 - b ^ 2 := by
  rw [ Nat.mul_comm, ← Nat.sq_sub_sq ]

/-
Fermat lensing as a compositeness certificate: if the two images `a-b`, `a+b`
are both nontrivial then their product `n` is composite.
-/
theorem composite_of_fermat (n a b : ℕ) (h : n = (a - b) * (a + b))
    (h1 : 1 < a - b) (h2 : a - b < n) : IsComposite n := by
  exact ⟨ a - b, h.symm ▸ dvd_mul_right _ _, h1, h2 ⟩

/-! ## §2. Pythagorean triples are natural lenses

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
Hypothesis: every Pythagorean triple is a *pre-built* lens. From `x²+y²=z²` we get
`x² = z² - y² = (z-y)(z+y)`, i.e. the square of a leg is lensed into the two images
`z-y` and `z+y`. The Berggren tree (catalog: BerggrenLorentz) generates infinitely
many such triples, hence infinitely many difference-of-squares factorizations of
leg-squares from the single seed (3,4,5).
Outcome: clean over `ℕ` once `y ≤ z` is supplied (always true for a triple).
-- !-- end -- !--
-/

/-
Every Pythagorean triple lenses the square of leg `x` into the two images
`z - y` and `z + y`.
-/
theorem pythag_leg_factor (x y z : ℕ) (h : x ^ 2 + y ^ 2 = z ^ 2) (hyz : y ≤ z) :
    (z - y) * (z + y) = x ^ 2 := by
  nlinarith [ Nat.sub_add_cancel hyz ]

/-! ## §3. The lens equation and the caustic: tropicalizing multiplication

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
Hypothesis: the `p`-adic valuation `v_p` is the deflection map of the lens of mass
`p`. The two universal laws of the lens are exactly the two structural maps of a
*tropical (min-plus) semiring*:
  • PRODUCT becomes SUM:  v_p(ab) = v_p a + v_p b   (tropical multiplication is `+`);
  • SUM is FOCUSED by MIN: min(v_p a, v_p b) ≤ v_p(a+b)  (tropical addition is `min`).
The second law is the ultrametric "caustic": superposed rays are never deflected
*less* than the least-deflected ray. This is the bridge to
`Bridges/CategoricalTropicalUltrametric.lean`.
Insight: the caustic law holds even when `a` or `b` is `0` thanks to the convention
`v_p 0 = 0`, but we keep `a,b ≠ 0` for the meaningful (genuinely lensed) regime.
-- !-- end -- !--
-/

variable {p : ℕ}

/-
**Lens equation (deflection adds).** Tropicalization of multiplication:
under the `p`-adic lens, a product of rays deflects by the sum of the deflections.
-/
theorem trop_lens_mul [Fact p.Prime] (a b : ℕ) (ha : a ≠ 0) (hb : b ≠ 0) :
    padicValNat p (a * b) = padicValNat p a + padicValNat p b := by
  rw [ padicValNat.mul ] <;> aesop

/-
**Caustic / strong-focusing law.** Tropicalization of addition: a superposition
of two rays is deflected at least as much as the least-deflected component.
-/
theorem trop_lens_caustic [Fact p.Prime] (a b : ℕ) (hab : a + b ≠ 0) :
    min (padicValNat p a) (padicValNat p b) ≤ padicValNat p (a + b) := by
  set k := min (padicValNat p a) (padicValNat p b) with hk
  have h1 : p ^ k ∣ a := dvd_trans (pow_dvd_pow p (min_le_left _ _)) pow_padicValNat_dvd
  have h2 : p ^ k ∣ b := dvd_trans (pow_dvd_pow p (min_le_right _ _)) pow_padicValNat_dvd
  exact (padicValNat_dvd_iff_le hab).mp (dvd_add h1 h2)

/-
The `p`-adic **lens metric** obeys the strong (ultrametric) triangle inequality:
the deflection of a sum never exceeds the larger of the two deflections. This is the
analytic face of the caustic law, stated with `padicNorm`.
-/
theorem lens_metric_ultrametric [Fact p.Prime] (q r : ℚ) :
    padicNorm p (q + r) ≤ max (padicNorm p q) (padicNorm p r) := by
  grind +suggestions

/-! ## §4. Lensed Pythagorean depth: factorization = tropical partition

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
Hypothesis (the synthesis): combining §2 and §3, the lensed square of a Pythagorean
leg carries an *even* total deflection `2·v_p(x)`, which is tropically partitioned
between the two images `z-y` and `z+y`:
      v_p(z-y) + v_p(z+y) = v_p((z-y)(z+y)) = v_p(x²) = 2·v_p(x).
Thus "factoring `x²` through the Pythagorean lens" is literally splitting an even
deflection into two summands — an additive (tropical) partition. More generally,
ANY factorization `n = a·b` is an additive partition of the depth `v_p n`
(`lens_depth_partition`), the discrete shadow of the lens equation.
Failure analysis: needs `x ≠ 0` (otherwise `v_p 0 = 0` and both sides vanish, still
true but degenerate) and `y < z` so both images are nonzero; we record both.
-- !-- end -- !--
-/

/-
The deflection of a square is twice the deflection: `v_p(x²) = 2·v_p(x)`.
-/
theorem padicValNat_sq [Fact p.Prime] (x : ℕ) (hx : x ≠ 0) :
    padicValNat p (x ^ 2) = 2 * padicValNat p x := by
  rw [ sq, padicValNat.mul hx hx ];
  ring

/-
**Lensed Pythagorean depth.** The total deflection of the two images of a
Pythagorean leg-square is even, equal to twice the deflection of the leg.
-/
theorem pythag_lens_depth [Fact p.Prime] (x y z : ℕ)
    (hx : x ≠ 0) (h : x ^ 2 + y ^ 2 = z ^ 2) (hyz : y < z) :
    padicValNat p ((z - y) * (z + y)) = 2 * padicValNat p x := by
  grind +suggestions

/-
**Factorization = tropical partition of depth.** Any factorization `n = a·b`
splits the lens depth `v_p n` into the two summands `v_p a` and `v_p b`.
-/
theorem lens_depth_partition [Fact p.Prime] (a b : ℕ) (ha : a ≠ 0) (hb : b ≠ 0) :
    ∃ i j, i + j = padicValNat p (a * b) ∧
      padicValNat p a = i ∧ padicValNat p b = j := by
  exact ⟨ _, _, by rw [ padicValNat.mul ha hb ], rfl, rfl ⟩

end Pythagorean.TropicalLensingFactorization

# The Discrete Hodge Laplacian, its Harmonic Space, and Diffusion Message Passing

This file gives a **self-contained Mathlib foundation** for the discrete Hodge program.
It works with a two-step cochain complex of finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces

    U --e--> V --d--> W

and studies the *Hodge Laplacian* on the middle space `V`,

    Δ = d* ∘ d + e ∘ e*,

where `d* = LinearMap.adjoint d` and `e* = LinearMap.adjoint e`.

The single organizing identity is the sum-of-squares **Dirichlet energy**

    ⟪Δ x, x⟫ = ‖d x‖² + ‖e* x‖²,

from which everything else follows:

* the harmonic space `ker Δ` is exactly the *closed-and-co-closed* cochains
  (`d x = 0 ∧ e* x = 0`);
* the Rayleigh quadratic form is strictly positive off `ker Δ`;
* `Δ` is self-adjoint, so its image lands in `(ker Δ)ᗮ`.

On the dynamical side, the explicit-Euler **diffusion step** `S = id − a·Δ`
fixes the harmonic space pointwise and *conserves the harmonic projection* along the
whole trajectory, `P (Sᵏ x) = P x`: diffusion never creates or destroys the
topological (harmonic) component, it only relaxes the exact / co-exact part.

This file is deliberately independent of the rest of the catalog (it imports only
Mathlib), repairing the previously non-elaborating `Hodge*` stack.

-- !-- Lab Notebook -- !--
Hypothesis:  For the two-step complex `U → V → W`, the Hodge Laplacian
  `Δ = d*d + e e*` should satisfy the Dirichlet identity `⟪Δx,x⟫ = ‖dx‖² + ‖e*x‖²`,
  which simultaneously makes `Δ` positive semidefinite, identifies its kernel with the
  closed-&-co-closed cochains, and (via self-adjointness) forces `range Δ ⊆ (ker Δ)ᗮ`.
  The diffusion step `S = id − aΔ` should then fix harmonics and conserve the harmonic
  projection at every depth.
Result:  Formalised and proved sorry-free.  `hodgeLap_isSymmetric` (self-adjoint),
  `hodgeLap_quadratic_form` (the Dirichlet identity), `hodgeLap_apply_eq_zero_iff`
  (harmonic ⇔ closed & co-closed), `hodgeLap_quadratic_eq_zero_iff` (strict positivity
  off the kernel), `hodgeLap_apply_mem_orthogonal_ker` (`Δx ⊥ ker Δ`),
  `diffStep_harmonic_fixed` / `diffStep_pow_harmonic_fixed` (harmonics are fixed at
  every depth), and `harmonicProjection_diffStep` / `harmonicProjection_diffStep_pow`
  (the harmonic projection is conserved along diffusion).
Insight:  Every analytic fact is a one-line consequence of the two adjunction lemmas
  `adjoint_inner_left/right` once the energy is written as a sum of squares; the
  dynamical facts then need only linearity of `Δ` and of the orthogonal projection,
  plus the symmetry-driven inclusion `Δx ∈ (ker Δ)ᗮ`.
Failure analysis:  Working with the inner-product energy `⟪v,v⟫` rather than `‖v‖`
  avoids `Real.sqrt`; phrasing the kernel characterisation through the quadratic form
  (`⟪Δx,x⟫ = 0 ↔ Δx = 0`) sidesteps any explicit eigenvalue bookkeeping.
-- !-- Lab Notebook -- !--
-/
import Mathlib

open scoped InnerProductSpace BigOperators

namespace HodgeLaplacianGreen

variable {U V W : Type*}
  [NormedAddCommGroup U] [InnerProductSpace ℝ U] [FiniteDimensional ℝ U]
  [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V] [FiniteDimensional ℝ V]
  [NormedAddCommGroup W] [InnerProductSpace ℝ W] [FiniteDimensional ℝ W]

/-- The discrete **Hodge Laplacian** of the two-step complex `U --e--> V --d--> W`,
acting on the middle space `V` by `Δ = d* ∘ d + e ∘ e*`. -/
noncomputable def hodgeLap (e : U →ₗ[ℝ] V) (d : V →ₗ[ℝ] W) : V →ₗ[ℝ] V :=
  LinearMap.adjoint d ∘ₗ d + e ∘ₗ LinearMap.adjoint e

variable (e : U →ₗ[ℝ] V) (d : V →ₗ[ℝ] W)

@[simp] theorem hodgeLap_apply (x : V) :
    hodgeLap e d x = LinearMap.adjoint d (d x) + e (LinearMap.adjoint e x) := by
  simp [hodgeLap]

/-
!-- comment: Expand `Δ` and move each summand across the relevant adjunction
(`adjoint_inner_left/right`) to land symmetrically on `x` and `y`. -- !--

The Hodge Laplacian is **self-adjoint**: `⟪Δ x, y⟫ = ⟪x, Δ y⟫`.
-/
theorem hodgeLap_isSymmetric : (hodgeLap e d).IsSymmetric := by
  intro x y;
  simp +decide only [hodgeLap, LinearMap.add_apply, LinearMap.comp_apply, inner_add_left,
      LinearMap.adjoint_inner_left];
  rw [ inner_add_right, LinearMap.adjoint_inner_right ];
  simp +decide [ ← LinearMap.adjoint_inner_left ]

/-
!-- comment: `⟪d*(dx),x⟫ = ⟪dx,dx⟫` and `⟪e(e*x),x⟫ = ⟪e*x,e*x⟫` by the two
adjunction lemmas; rewrite `⟪v,v⟫` as `‖v‖²`. -- !--

The **Dirichlet energy / Rayleigh quotient** is a sum of squares:
`⟪Δ x, x⟫ = ‖d x‖² + ‖e* x‖²`.
-/
theorem hodgeLap_quadratic_form (x : V) :
    (⟪hodgeLap e d x, x⟫_ℝ) = ‖d x‖ ^ 2 + ‖LinearMap.adjoint e x‖ ^ 2 := by
  have h1 : ⟪LinearMap.adjoint d (d x), x⟫_ℝ = ‖d x‖ ^ 2 := by
    rw [LinearMap.adjoint_inner_left, real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq]
  have h2 : ⟪e (LinearMap.adjoint e x), x⟫_ℝ = ‖LinearMap.adjoint e x‖ ^ 2 := by
    rw [← LinearMap.adjoint_inner_right, real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq]
  simp only [hodgeLap, LinearMap.add_apply, LinearMap.comp_apply, inner_add_left, h1, h2]

/-
!-- comment: From the sum-of-squares form, `⟪Δx,x⟫ = 0` forces both squares to vanish;
conversely if both vanish then `Δx = 0`.  Combine with the quadratic-eq-zero lemma. -- !--

**Harmonic ⇔ closed & co-closed**: `Δ x = 0 ↔ d x = 0 ∧ e* x = 0`.
-/
theorem hodgeLap_apply_eq_zero_iff (x : V) :
    hodgeLap e d x = 0 ↔ d x = 0 ∧ LinearMap.adjoint e x = 0 := by
  by_cases h₁ : d x = 0 <;> simp_all +decide [ hodgeLap ];
  · constructor <;> intro h <;> have := LinearMap.adjoint_inner_right e ( LinearMap.adjoint e x ) x <;> simp_all +decide [ inner_self_eq_norm_sq_to_K ];
  · contrapose! h₁; have := hodgeLap_quadratic_form e d x; simp_all +decide;
    exact norm_eq_zero.mp ( by nlinarith )

/-
!-- comment: `⟪Δx,x⟫ = ‖dx‖²+‖e*x‖² = 0 ↔ dx = 0 ∧ e*x = 0 ↔ Δx = 0`
(strict positivity of the Rayleigh form off the kernel). -- !--

**Strict positivity off the kernel**: the Rayleigh form vanishes only on harmonics,
`⟪Δ x, x⟫ = 0 ↔ Δ x = 0`.
-/
theorem hodgeLap_quadratic_eq_zero_iff (x : V) :
    (⟪hodgeLap e d x, x⟫_ℝ) = 0 ↔ hodgeLap e d x = 0 := by
  convert ( hodgeLap_apply_eq_zero_iff e d x ) |> Iff.symm using 1;
  rw [ hodgeLap_quadratic_form ];
  exact ⟨ fun h => ⟨ norm_eq_zero.mp ( by nlinarith ), norm_eq_zero.mp ( by nlinarith ) ⟩, fun h => by simp +decide [ h ] ⟩

/-
!-- comment: For `h ∈ ker Δ`, `⟪h, Δx⟫ = ⟪Δh, x⟫ = 0` by self-adjointness, so
`Δx ⊥ ker Δ`. -- !--

**Image lands in the orthogonal complement of the kernel**: `Δ x ∈ (ker Δ)ᗮ`.
-/
theorem hodgeLap_apply_mem_orthogonal_ker (x : V) :
    hodgeLap e d x ∈ (LinearMap.ker (hodgeLap e d))ᗮ := by
  intro y hy;
  convert congr_arg ( fun z => ⟪z, x⟫_ℝ ) hy using 1;
  · rw [ hodgeLap_isSymmetric ];
  · simp +decide

/-! ## Diffusion message passing -/

/-- One explicit-Euler **diffusion step** `S = id − a·Δ`, as a linear endomorphism of
`V`, so that iterating it (`S ^ k`) is automatically linear. -/
noncomputable def diffStep (a : ℝ) : V →ₗ[ℝ] V :=
  LinearMap.id - a • hodgeLap e d

@[simp] theorem diffStep_apply (a : ℝ) (x : V) :
    diffStep e d a x = x - a • hodgeLap e d x := by
  simp [diffStep]

/-- The **harmonic projection** `P`: orthogonal projection onto the harmonic space
`ker Δ`. -/
noncomputable def harmonicProjection : V →L[ℝ] (LinearMap.ker (hodgeLap e d)) :=
  (LinearMap.ker (hodgeLap e d)).orthogonalProjection

/-
!-- comment: If `Δh = 0` then `S h = h − a•0 = h`. -- !--

Harmonic cochains are **fixed points** of a diffusion step.
-/
theorem diffStep_harmonic_fixed (a : ℝ) {h : V} (hh : hodgeLap e d h = 0) :
    diffStep e d a h = h := by
  unfold diffStep; aesop;

/-
!-- comment: Iterate `diffStep_harmonic_fixed` over depth `k` by induction
(`pow_succ'`). -- !--

Harmonic cochains are fixed at **every depth** of diffusion.
-/
theorem diffStep_pow_harmonic_fixed (a : ℝ) {h : V} (hh : hodgeLap e d h = 0) (k : ℕ) :
    ((diffStep e d a) ^ k) h = h := by
  induction' k with k ih;
  · rfl;
  · rw [ pow_succ', Module.End.mul_apply, ih, diffStep_harmonic_fixed e d a hh ]

/-
!-- comment: `S x = x − a•Δx` and `Δx ∈ (ker Δ)ᗮ`, so projecting kills the second
term: `P(Sx) = Px − a•P(Δx) = Px`. -- !--

**Conservation of the harmonic projection** under one diffusion step:
`P (S x) = P x`.
-/
theorem harmonicProjection_diffStep (a : ℝ) (x : V) :
    harmonicProjection e d (diffStep e d a x) = harmonicProjection e d x := by
  have h_orthogonal : ∀ (v : V), v ∈ (LinearMap.ker (hodgeLap e d))ᗮ → (harmonicProjection e d) v = 0 := by
    simp +decide [ harmonicProjection ];
  rw [ diffStep_apply, map_sub, map_smul, h_orthogonal _ ( hodgeLap_apply_mem_orthogonal_ker e d x ), smul_zero, sub_zero ]

/-
!-- comment: Induct on depth using the single-step conservation
`harmonicProjection_diffStep`. -- !--

**Conservation of the harmonic projection along the whole trajectory**:
`P (Sᵏ x) = P x`.
-/
theorem harmonicProjection_diffStep_pow (a : ℝ) (x : V) (k : ℕ) :
    harmonicProjection e d (((diffStep e d a) ^ k) x) = harmonicProjection e d x := by
  induction' k with k ih;
  · rfl;
  · convert harmonicProjection_diffStep e d a ( ( diffStep e d a ^ k ) x ) using 1;
    · exact congr_arg _ ( by rw [ pow_succ', Module.End.mul_apply ] );
    · exact ih.symm

end HodgeLaplacianGreen

# Future Directions — Discrete Hodge Laplacian, Harmonic Space & Diffusion Message Passing

## Synthesis

This cycle rebuilds the discrete Hodge program on a **self-contained Mathlib foundation**.
The previous catalog `Hodge*` stack did not elaborate: `HodgeMessagePassingConvergence`
imports a module `Speculative.AutoResearch.HodgeSpectralThreshold` that does not exist in the
repository, and the package declared no `srcDir`, so `lake` could not even locate the catalog
sources. Two infrastructure repairs were made — adding `srcDir = "Catalog"` to `lakefile.toml`
so module resolution works at all — and a new, dependency-free file
`Catalog/Speculative/AutoResearch/HodgeLaplacianGreen.lean` re-derives the operator-algebra,
analytic, and dynamical layers of the program from Mathlib alone.

The central object is the discrete **Hodge Laplacian** of a two-step cochain complex of
finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces

```
U --e--> V --d--> W ,        Δ = d* ∘ d + e ∘ e*   on   V ,
```

with `d* = LinearMap.adjoint d` and `e* = LinearMap.adjoint e`. The single organizing identity
is the sum-of-squares **Dirichlet energy**

```
⟪Δ x, x⟫ = ‖d x‖² + ‖e* x‖² ,
```

from which everything else follows. The harmonic space `ker Δ` is exactly the
closed-and-co-closed cochains (`d x = 0 ∧ e* x = 0`); the Rayleigh form is strictly positive
off `ker Δ`; self-adjointness places the image of `Δ` inside `(ker Δ)ᗮ`. On the dynamical
side, the explicit-Euler diffusion step `S = id − a·Δ` fixes the harmonic space pointwise and
conserves the harmonic projection along the whole trajectory, `P (Sᵏ x) = P x`: diffusion
never creates or destroys the topological (harmonic) component, it only relaxes the
exact / co-exact part. This is the local-to-global picture made discrete: local data (the maps
`d`, `e` on individual cochains) glues, via the Hodge decomposition, into the global
obstruction object `ker Δ`.

## Results summary (proved sorry-free; axioms `propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound`)

| Theorem | Statement |
|---|---|
| `hodgeLap_isSymmetric` | `Δ` is self-adjoint |
| `hodgeLap_quadratic_form` | `⟪Δ x, x⟫ = ‖d x‖² + ‖e* x‖²` |
| `hodgeLap_apply_eq_zero_iff` | `Δ x = 0 ↔ d x = 0 ∧ e* x = 0` (harmonic ⇔ closed & co-closed) |
| `hodgeLap_quadratic_eq_zero_iff` | `⟪Δ x, x⟫ = 0 ↔ Δ x = 0` (strict positivity off the kernel) |
| `hodgeLap_apply_mem_orthogonal_ker` | `Δ x ∈ (ker Δ)ᗮ` |
| `diffStep_harmonic_fixed` / `diffStep_pow_harmonic_fixed` | `Sᵏ h = h` for harmonic `h` |
| `harmonicProjection_diffStep` / `harmonicProjection_diffStep_pow` | `P (Sᵏ x) = P x` |

## Research directions

### 1. From "image in `(ker Δ)ᗮ`" to the orthogonal splitting `range Δ = (ker Δ)ᗮ`
This cycle proves the easy inclusion `Δ x ∈ (ker Δ)ᗮ` (`hodgeLap_apply_mem_orthogonal_ker`).
Conjecture the full identity `range Δ = (ker Δ)ᗮ`, and consequently that `Δ` is a linear
isomorphism of `(ker Δ)ᗮ` onto itself. Falsifiable by any `y ∈ (ker Δ)ᗮ` not of the form
`Δ x`, or any nonzero `z ∈ (ker Δ)ᗮ` with `Δ z = 0`. **The key insight is** that injectivity
on the complement is immediate from strict positivity — if `z ∈ (ker Δ)ᗮ` and `Δ z = 0` then
`z ∈ ker Δ ∩ (ker Δ)ᗮ = 0` — and in finite dimensions an injective self-map of `(ker Δ)ᗮ` is
surjective, so the rank–nullity count `dim(range Δ) = dim V − dim(ker Δ) = dim (ker Δ)ᗮ`
closes the inclusion to an equality. **Why now?** Self-adjointness, strict positivity, and the
membership lemma are all theorems this cycle, so the remaining step is a dimension count using
Mathlib's `LinearMap.finrank_range_add_finrank_ker` and `Submodule.finrank_add_finrank_orthogonal`.

### 2. Bundle the Green's operator into an honest self-adjoint linear map
With Direction 1 in hand, every `x` has a unique `z ∈ (ker Δ)ᗮ` with `Δ z = x − P x`.
Conjecture this assembles into a genuine `G : V →ₗ[ℝ] V` with `Δ ∘ G = G ∘ Δ = id − P`,
`G ∘ P = 0`, and `G` self-adjoint (`⟪G x, y⟫ = ⟪x, G y⟫`). Falsifiable by a candidate `G` with
`Δ (G x) ≠ x − P x` on some `x`, or with `⟪G x, y⟫ ≠ ⟪x, G y⟫`. **The key insight is** that
uniqueness is the *only* obstruction to linearity of a solver: `z(x+y)` and `z(x)+z(y)` solve
the same problem, so injectivity on `(ker Δ)ᗮ` forces them equal, making
`G x := Classical.choose …` automatically additive and homogeneous, with `LinearMap.mk` closing
the construction. **Why now?** Direction 1 supplies the existence-and-uniqueness needed; each
`LinearMap` axiom is then a one-line uniqueness argument, and self-adjointness follows from
`hodgeLap_isSymmetric` restricted to the invariant complement.

### 3. The diffusion energy is a strict Lyapunov function with harmonic limit
Conjecture the Dirichlet energy `E(x) = ⟪Δ x, x⟫` is non-increasing along admissible diffusion,
`E(S x) ≤ E(x)` for `0 < a < 2/λ_max`, with equality iff `x` is harmonic, and that `Sᵏ x → P x`
as `k → ∞`. Falsifiable by an `x` and admissible `a` with `E(S x) > E(x)`, or a non-harmonic
fixed point of `S`. **The key insight is** that `hodgeLap_quadratic_form` already exhibits `E`
as a sum of squares whose zero set is exactly `ker Δ` (`hodgeLap_quadratic_eq_zero_iff`), and
`harmonicProjection_diffStep_pow` pins the limit's harmonic part to `P x`, so only the
complementary part must be shown to vanish. **Why now?** Both the Lyapunov candidate (the proven
quadratic form) and the conserved target (`P x`) are in hand; monotonicity reduces to the single
algebraic estimate `E(x) − E(Sx) = 2a⟪Δx,Δx⟫ − a²⟪Δx,Δ(Δx)⟫ ≥ 0` once `Δ` is bounded by `λ_max`
on the complement.

### 4. Spectral resolution `Δ = Σ λᵢ Pᵢ` with `P₀ = P` and `G = Σ_{λᵢ>0} λᵢ⁻¹ Pᵢ`
Conjecture the finite-dimensional spectral theorem for `Δ`: an orthonormal eigenbasis with
`0 = λ₀ ≤ λ₁ ≤ …`, the `0`-eigenprojection equal to the harmonic projection `P`, `Δ = Σ λᵢ Pᵢ`,
and the Green's operator of Direction 2 equal to `G = Σ_{λᵢ>0} λᵢ⁻¹ Pᵢ`. Falsifiable by a
negative eigenvalue, a non-harmonic `0`-eigenvector, or a mismatch `G ≠ Σ λᵢ⁻¹ Pᵢ`. **The key
insight is** that `hodgeLap_isSymmetric` feeds Mathlib's finite-dimensional spectral theorem
directly, the quadratic form pins the spectrum to `[0, ∞)`, and `hodgeLap_quadratic_eq_zero_iff`
identifies the `0`-eigenspace with `ker Δ`, so the eigendecomposition is an *application* rather
than a new theory. **Why now?** All three hypotheses of the spectral theorem are theorems this
cycle, and Direction 2's Green operator forces the inverse-eigenvalue formula once the
eigenprojections exist; the contraction rate `ρ = max_{λ>0} |1 − aλ|` of diffusion then drops out
per eigenvector.

### 5. The discrete Hodge isomorphism `ker d / range e ≃ ker Δ` as a quotient isometry
Conjecture that the harmonic representative realizes the cohomology quotient: every closed class
`[x]` (with `d x = 0`) has a unique harmonic representative `P x ∈ ker Δ`, giving a linear
isomorphism `ker d / range e ≃ ker Δ` that is moreover an **isometry** for the quotient norm,
`‖[x]‖ = ‖P x‖`. (This direction needs the cochain condition `d ∘ e = 0`, which the present file
does not yet assume.) Falsifiable by a closed `x` whose harmonic projection leaves the class, or a
class whose quotient norm differs from `‖P x‖`. **The key insight is** that Direction 1's splitting
`range Δ = (ker Δ)ᗮ` separates any closed cochain into a harmonic part `P x` and a part in
`range Δ = range d* ⊕ range e`; restricted to closed cochains the `d*`-component vanishes, so
`x − P x ∈ range e` and `P x` is the canonical representative, with `‖P x‖ ≤ ‖x − e u‖` making the
quotient infimum attained exactly at `P x`. **Why now?** The orthogonal splitting and harmonic
projection identities are (or shortly will be) theorems; only the identification of Mathlib's
`Submodule.Quotient.norm_mk` infimum with this attained minimum remains to upgrade the linear iso
to a `LinearIsometryEquiv`.

# Two-way independence model: the algebra of `2 × 2` basic moves

This file develops the *algebraic foundation* for the study of Markov bases of the
two-way independence model of contingency tables.

A contingency table is an `m × n` array of nonnegative integers.  In algebraic
statistics one fixes the *margins* (row sums and column sums) of a table and asks
which tables share those margins; the set of all such tables is the *fiber*.  The
classical theorem of Diaconis–Sturmfels says that for the two-way independence
model the fiber is connected by the *basic moves*
`B(i,i',j,j') = e_{i,j'} + e_{i',j} - e_{i,j} - e_{i',j'}` (for `i ≠ i'`,
`j ≠ j'`), i.e. one can walk between any two tables of the same margins using a
sequence of these `± 1` adjustments to a `2 × 2` sub-rectangle while staying
nonnegative.

## Scope

This file is deliberately limited to the *soundness* direction of the theory and
the algebraic bookkeeping that supports it:

* a basic move never changes any row sum or column sum (so it preserves the
  fiber), and its total sum is zero;
* the one-step legal move relation `LegalBasicStep` (which additionally records
  that both endpoints are entrywise nonnegative) keeps two tables in the same
  fiber;
* the "kernel" lemma that two equal-margin tables differ by something with all
  row sums and column sums equal to zero.

It does **not** prove the full connectivity (completeness) theorem that *every*
pair of equal-margin nonnegative tables is connected by basic moves.  The API
here is intended to be a stable, reusable basis for such a later development.

## Main definitions

* `MarkovBases.TwoWay.Table m n` — an `m × n` integer table.
* `rowSum`, `colSum`, `totalSum` — the marginals and the grand total.
* `sameMargins` — two tables agree on all row and column sums.
* `basicMove i i' j j'` — the elementary `2 × 2` move.
* `Nonneg` — entrywise nonnegativity.
* `LegalBasicStep` — the one-step move relation.

## Main results

* `basicMove_rowSum`, `basicMove_colSum` — a basic move has all row/column sums `0`.
* `basicMove_totalSum_zero` — a basic move has total sum `0`.
* `basicMove_sameMargins` — adding a basic move preserves all margins.
* `LegalBasicStep.sameMargins` — a legal step connects tables in the same fiber.
* `sameMargins_sub` — equal margins force the difference to have zero marginals.
-/

import Mathlib

namespace MarkovBases.TwoWay

/-- An `m × n` integer contingency table.  Entry `T i j` is the count in row `i`
and column `j`.  We work over `ℤ` so that differences of tables (and the basic
moves) live in the same type; nonnegativity is tracked separately by `Nonneg`. -/
abbrev Table (m n : ℕ) := Fin m → Fin n → ℤ

/-- The `i`-th **row sum** (row marginal) of a table. -/
def rowSum {m n : ℕ} (T : Table m n) (i : Fin m) : ℤ := ∑ j, T i j

/-- The `j`-th **column sum** (column marginal) of a table. -/
def colSum {m n : ℕ} (T : Table m n) (j : Fin n) : ℤ := ∑ i, T i j

/-- The **grand total** of a table, computed as the sum of its row sums. -/
def totalSum {m n : ℕ} (T : Table m n) : ℤ := ∑ i, rowSum T i

/-- Two tables have the **same margins** when they agree on every row sum and on
every column sum.  The fiber over a fixed margin is exactly an equivalence class
of this relation (restricted to nonnegative tables). -/
def sameMargins {m n : ℕ} (T S : Table m n) : Prop :=
  (∀ i, rowSum T i = rowSum S i) ∧ (∀ j, colSum T j = colSum S j)

/-- The elementary **basic move** `B(i,i',j,j') = e_{i,j'} + e_{i',j} - e_{i,j} -
e_{i',j'}`.

As a table it adds `1` to the `(i,j')` and `(i',j)` cells and subtracts `1` from
the `(i,j)` and `(i',j')` cells, i.e. it rotates `± 1` around the `2 × 2`
sub-rectangle with rows `i, i'` and columns `j, j'`.  The definition does not
require `i ≠ i'` or `j ≠ j'`; the marginal-preservation lemmas below hold for all
indices, and the genuine "non-degenerate" requirement is imposed where it matters
in `LegalBasicStep`. -/
def basicMove {m n : ℕ} (i i' : Fin m) (j j' : Fin n) : Table m n :=
  fun a b =>
    (if a = i ∧ b = j' then 1 else 0)
    + (if a = i' ∧ b = j then 1 else 0)
    - (if a = i ∧ b = j then 1 else 0)
    - (if a = i' ∧ b = j' then 1 else 0)

/-- Summing a single "indicator" `e_{i,j'}` along a row collapses to the row
indicator `[a = i]`. -/
private lemma sum_col_ite {m n : ℕ} (i : Fin m) (j' : Fin n) (a : Fin m) :
    ∑ b : Fin n, (if a = i ∧ b = j' then (1 : ℤ) else 0) = if a = i then 1 else 0 := by
  by_cases h : a = i <;> simp [h]

/-- Summing a single "indicator" `e_{i,j'}` along a column collapses to the column
indicator `[b = j']`. -/
private lemma sum_row_ite {m n : ℕ} (i : Fin m) (j' : Fin n) (b : Fin n) :
    ∑ a : Fin m, (if a = i ∧ b = j' then (1 : ℤ) else 0) = if b = j' then 1 else 0 := by
  by_cases h : b = j' <;> simp [h, and_comm]

/-- Row sums are additive in the table. -/
theorem rowSum_add {m n : ℕ} (T S : Table m n) (i : Fin m) :
    rowSum (T + S) i = rowSum T i + rowSum S i := by
  simp [rowSum, Finset.sum_add_distrib]

/-- Column sums are additive in the table. -/
theorem colSum_add {m n : ℕ} (T S : Table m n) (j : Fin n) :
    colSum (T + S) j = colSum T j + colSum S j := by
  simp [colSum, Finset.sum_add_distrib]

/-- Row sums respect subtraction of tables. -/
theorem rowSum_sub {m n : ℕ} (T S : Table m n) (i : Fin m) :
    rowSum (T - S) i = rowSum T i - rowSum S i := by
  simp [rowSum, Finset.sum_sub_distrib]

/-- Column sums respect subtraction of tables. -/
theorem colSum_sub {m n : ℕ} (T S : Table m n) (j : Fin n) :
    colSum (T - S) j = colSum T j - colSum S j := by
  simp [colSum, Finset.sum_sub_distrib]

/-- **Every row sum of a basic move is zero.**  The `+1` at `(i,j')` and the `-1`
at `(i,j)` cancel within row `i`, and likewise the `+1` at `(i',j)` and `-1` at
`(i',j')` cancel within row `i'`; all other rows are empty.  This holds for all
indices, even degenerate ones. -/
theorem basicMove_rowSum {m n : ℕ} (i i' : Fin m) (j j' : Fin n) (a : Fin m) :
    rowSum (basicMove i i' j j') a = 0 := by
  simp only [rowSum, basicMove, Finset.sum_sub_distrib, Finset.sum_add_distrib,
    sum_col_ite]
  ring

/-- **Every column sum of a basic move is zero.**  Dual to `basicMove_rowSum`. -/
theorem basicMove_colSum {m n : ℕ} (i i' : Fin m) (j j' : Fin n) (b : Fin n) :
    colSum (basicMove i i' j j') b = 0 := by
  simp only [colSum, basicMove, Finset.sum_sub_distrib, Finset.sum_add_distrib,
    sum_row_ite]
  ring

/-- **The total sum of a basic move is zero.**  Immediate from
`basicMove_rowSum`, since the grand total is the sum of the (all-zero) row sums. -/
theorem basicMove_totalSum_zero {m n : ℕ} (i i' : Fin m) (j j' : Fin n) :
    totalSum (basicMove i i' j j') = 0 := by
  simp [totalSum, basicMove_rowSum]

/-- **Adding a basic move preserves every margin.**  Hence `T` and
`T + basicMove i i' j j'` lie in the same fiber.  (Stated with `T + move` on the
left so that it reads "the moved table has the same margins as the original".) -/
theorem basicMove_sameMargins {m n : ℕ} (T : Table m n) (i i' : Fin m) (j j' : Fin n) :
    sameMargins (T + basicMove i i' j j') T := by
  refine ⟨fun a => ?_, fun b => ?_⟩
  · rw [rowSum_add, basicMove_rowSum]; ring
  · rw [colSum_add, basicMove_colSum]; ring

/-- A table is **nonnegative** when all of its entries are `≥ 0`, i.e. it is a
genuine array of counts. -/
def Nonneg {m n : ℕ} (T : Table m n) : Prop := ∀ a b, 0 ≤ T a b

/-- The **legal one-step move** relation: `LegalBasicStep u v` holds when `v` is
obtained from `u` by adding a non-degenerate basic move (`i ≠ i'`, `j ≠ j'`) and
both `u` and `v` are nonnegative tables.  These are the edges of the Markov
graph on a fiber. -/
def LegalBasicStep {m n : ℕ} (u v : Table m n) : Prop :=
  ∃ (i i' : Fin m) (j j' : Fin n),
    i ≠ i' ∧ j ≠ j' ∧ v = u + basicMove i i' j j' ∧ Nonneg u ∧ Nonneg v

/-- **Soundness of one legal step.**  A legal basic move connects two tables in
the same fiber: if `LegalBasicStep u v` then `u` and `v` have the same margins.
This is the "easy" half of fiber connectivity, and the part this file is about. -/
theorem LegalBasicStep.sameMargins {m n : ℕ} {u v : Table m n}
    (h : LegalBasicStep u v) : sameMargins u v := by
  obtain ⟨i, i', j, j', _, _, hv, _, _⟩ := h
  subst hv
  refine ⟨fun a => ?_, fun b => ?_⟩
  · rw [rowSum_add, basicMove_rowSum]; ring
  · rw [colSum_add, basicMove_colSum]; ring

/-- **Kernel lemma.**  If `u` and `v` have the same margins then their difference
`u - v` lies in the lattice kernel of the margin map: all of its row sums and all
of its column sums vanish.  This is the algebraic object whose lattice of moves
the basic moves are meant to generate. -/
theorem sameMargins_sub {m n : ℕ} {u v : Table m n} (h : sameMargins u v) :
    (∀ i, rowSum (u - v) i = 0) ∧ (∀ j, colSum (u - v) j = 0) := by
  obtain ⟨hr, hc⟩ := h
  refine ⟨fun i => ?_, fun j => ?_⟩
  · rw [rowSum_sub, hr]; ring
  · rw [colSum_sub, hc]; ring

end MarkovBases.TwoWay

import Mathlib
import Catalog.Logic.HoTT.IdentitySystems

universe u v w u' v'

namespace HoTTFound

variable {A : Sort u} {a₀ : A} {R : A → Sort v}

/-! ## Direction 1: the converse / characterisation -/

-- !-- A fibrewise family of equivalences assembles into one equivalence of
-- total spaces, acting as the identity on the base and the given equivalence on
-- each fibre. -- !--
/-- Fibrewise equivalences assemble into an equivalence of dependent-sum total
    spaces. This is the `Σ'`-congruence rule for `Equiv'`, the engine behind the
    converse and closure properties below. -/
def Equiv'.psigmaCongr {A : Sort u} {P : A → Sort v} {Q : A → Sort w}
    (e : ∀ a, P a ≃' Q a) : (Σ' a, P a) ≃' (Σ' a, Q a) where
  toFun := fun s => ⟨s.1, (e s.1).toFun s.2⟩
  invFun := fun s => ⟨s.1, (e s.1).invFun s.2⟩
  left_inv := fun ⟨a, x⟩ => by simp [(e a).left_inv]
  right_inv := fun ⟨a, y⟩ => by simp [(e a).right_inv]

-- !-- Push the contractibility of the based path total space `Σ' a, (a₀ = a)`
-- across the assembled fibrewise equivalence; the centre lands on `⟨a₀, e rfl⟩`,
-- which is exactly the required reflexivity witness, so `center_eq` is `rfl`. -- !--
/-- **Converse of the fundamental theorem (Direction 1).**

    If a family `R` is fibrewise equivalent to the based path family `a₀ = ·`,
    then `R` *is* an identity system based at `a₀` (with reflexivity witness the
    image of `rfl`). Combined with `fundamentalIdentitySystem` this characterises
    identity systems: `R` is an identity system iff it is fibrewise equivalent to
    the based path family. -/
def idSys_of_fiber_equiv (e : ∀ a, (a₀ = a) ≃' R a) : IdentitySystem A a₀ R where
  rflR := (e a₀).toFun rfl
  contr_total := Equiv'.contractible (Equiv'.psigmaCongr e) (contractible_based_paths a₀)
  center_eq := rfl

/-! ## Direction 4: the induced eliminator (path induction) -/

-- !-- A transport in a `Prop`-valued `Eq` along a loop `pf : x = x` is the
-- identity, because `pf = rfl` by proof irrelevance. -- !--
/-- Transport (`Eq.mpr ∘ congrArg`) along a *loop* is the identity. The technical
    engine for the eliminator's computation rule. -/
theorem mpr_congr_loop {X : Sort u} {x : X} {D : X → Sort w} (pf : x = x) (d : D x) :
    Eq.mpr (congrArg D pf) d = d := by
  have h : pf = rfl := proof_irrel _ _
  subst h
  rfl

-- !-- Given `r : R a`, the contractibility of `Σ' a, R a` makes `⟨a, r⟩` equal to
-- the centre `⟨a₀, rflR⟩`; transport the base datum `d` along that equality in the
-- total space. -- !--
/-- **The eliminator induced by an identity system (Direction 4).**

    Every identity system induces a dependent eliminator: to define a section of
    any `D : ∀ a, R a → Sort w` it suffices to give its value `d` on the
    reflexivity witness. This is the analogue of path induction (`Eq.rec`) for the
    family `R`. -/
def idSysElim (S : IdentitySystem A a₀ R) (D : (a : A) → R a → Sort w)
    (d : D a₀ S.rflR) (a : A) (r : R a) : D a r :=
  Eq.mpr (congrArg (fun s : Σ' x, R x => D s.1 s.2)
    ((S.contr_total.contr ⟨a, r⟩).trans S.center_eq)) d

-- !-- At the reflexivity witness the relevant transport is along a loop, hence
-- the identity by `mpr_congr_loop`. -- !--
/-- **Computation rule for the induced eliminator.**

    On the reflexivity witness, the eliminator reduces to the supplied base case,
    exactly as `Eq.rec` reduces on `rfl`. -/
theorem idSysElim_beta (S : IdentitySystem A a₀ R) (D : (a : A) → R a → Sort w)
    (d : D a₀ S.rflR) : idSysElim S D d a₀ S.rflR = d := by
  unfold idSysElim
  exact mpr_congr_loop (D := fun s : Σ' x, R x => D s.1 s.2)
    ((S.contr_total.contr ⟨a₀, S.rflR⟩).trans S.center_eq) d

/-! ## Direction 5: the bridge to Mathlib's `Equiv` -/

-- !-- The two roundtrip laws of `Equiv'` are definitionally Mathlib's
-- `left_inv`/`right_inv`, so this is a pure repackaging. -- !--
/-- The catalog's bespoke `Equiv'` forgets to a genuine Mathlib `Equiv`. -/
def Equiv'.toEquiv {α : Sort u} {β : Sort v} (e : α ≃' β) : α ≃ β :=
  ⟨e.toFun, e.invFun, e.left_inv, e.right_inv⟩

-- !-- Apply the forgetful bridge to the fundamental equivalence of the previous
-- cycle. -- !--
/-- **The fundamental theorem, exported to Mathlib (Direction 5).**

    The fundamental equivalence of an identity system as a Mathlib `Equiv`
    `(a₀ = a) ≃ R a`, making every catalog identity-system result importable into
    mainstream Mathlib developments (transport, `Equiv.subsingleton`, …). -/
def fundamentalIdentitySystemEquiv (S : IdentitySystem A a₀ R) (a : A) :
    (a₀ = a) ≃ R a :=
  (fundamentalIdentitySystem S a).toEquiv

/-! ## Direction 3: closure under products -/

-- !-- The centre is the pair of centres; any pair equals it componentwise. -- !--
/-- The product of two contractible types is contractible. -/
def Contractible.prod {α : Type u} {β : Type v}
    (h : Contractible α) (h' : Contractible β) : Contractible (α × β) where
  center := (h.center, h'.center)
  contr := fun y => by cases y; simp [h.contr, h'.contr]

-- !-- Reassociate `Σ' (p : A × A'), R p.1 × R' p.2` with the product of the two
-- separate total spaces; both roundtrips are `rfl`. -- !--
/-- The total space of the product family regroups into the product of the two
    total spaces. The `Σ'`-distribution equivalence over a product base. -/
def Equiv'.sigmaProd {A : Type u} {A' : Type u'} {R : A → Type v} {R' : A' → Type v'} :
    (Σ' (p : A × A'), R p.1 × R' p.2) ≃' ((Σ' a, R a) × (Σ' a', R' a')) where
  toFun := fun s => (⟨s.1.1, s.2.1⟩, ⟨s.1.2, s.2.2⟩)
  invFun := fun s => ⟨(s.1.1, s.2.1), s.1.2, s.2.2⟩
  left_inv := fun ⟨⟨_, _⟩, _, _⟩ => rfl
  right_inv := fun (⟨_, _⟩, ⟨_, _⟩) => rfl

-- !-- Contractibility of the product total space transports from the product of
-- contractibilities across `sigmaProd.symm`; the centre then reduces to the pair
-- of reflexivity witnesses by `center_eq` of each factor. -- !--
/-- **Closure of identity systems under products (Direction 3).**

    The product of two identity systems is an identity system on the product
    type, with the pointwise product family and the pair of reflexivity
    witnesses. -/
def idSys_prod {A : Type u} {a₀ : A} {R : A → Type v}
    {A' : Type u'} {a₀' : A'} {R' : A' → Type v'}
    (S : IdentitySystem A a₀ R) (S' : IdentitySystem A' a₀' R') :
    IdentitySystem (A × A') (a₀, a₀') (fun p => R p.1 × R' p.2) where
  rflR := (S.rflR, S'.rflR)
  contr_total := Equiv'.contractible Equiv'.sigmaProd.symm
    (Contractible.prod S.contr_total S'.contr_total)
  center_eq := by
    simp only [Equiv'.contractible, Equiv'.symm, Equiv'.sigmaProd, Contractible.prod]
    rw [S.center_eq, S'.center_eq]

end HoTTFound

/-! # Density along the whole height ladder of p-degrees

This file is a **fifth-cycle** companion to the order-type development.  `OrderType.lean`
exhibited a *single* density witness `interSys`, strictly between `linSystem` and
`fibSystem`.  `DegreeLattice.lean` built the infinite height ladder `powSystem k`
(size `2 ^ (n ^ k)`) with `powSystem k < powSystem (k+1)` for `k ≥ 1`.

Here we prove **density at every rung of the ladder simultaneously**: between any two
consecutive ladder degrees there is a strictly intermediate p-degree
(`exists_strictly_between_powSystem`).  The witness `interPowSys k` is the *parity-glued*
size function that runs the upper rate `2 ^ (n ^ (k+1))` on the even indices and the lower
rate `2 ^ (n ^ k)` on the odd indices: super-polynomially above the lower rung (the even
indices keep the faster rate), yet too thin to recover the upper rung (the odd indices fall
back to the slower rate).  This is a *local-to-global* glueing: a degree is assembled from
the two rates prescribed on the two residue classes mod 2.

The engine is the domination characterisation `simulates_sysOfSize_iff` together with the
uniform gap `pow_pow_succ_gap_strong`, an "all-large-`n`" strengthening of
`DegreeLattice.pow_pow_succ_gap` that lets us select a witness of prescribed parity.

-- !-- Lab Notebook -- !--
Hypothesis : The single Fibonacci-vs-linear density witness should generalise to *every*
             consecutive pair `powSystem k < powSystem (k+1)` on the height ladder, via the
             same parity-thinning trick applied to the ladder's exponents.
Result     : Confirmed, `sorry = 0`.  `interPowSys k` lies strictly between `powSystem k`
             and `powSystem (k+1)` for every `k ≥ 1` (`powSystem_lt_interPow`,
             `interPow_lt_powSystem_succ`, `exists_strictly_between_powSystem`).
Insight    : Whereas `DegreeLattice.pow_pow_succ_gap` only produced *one* exponent `n`
             realising the super-polynomial gap, density needs a gap witness of a *chosen
             parity*.  Strengthening to "the gap holds for **all** `n ≥ c + 2`"
             (`pow_pow_succ_gap_strong`) makes the parity free: pick an even or odd witness
             above the threshold as needed.  The clean bound is
             `(2^(n^k)+2)^c ≤ 2^(c·n^k + c) < 2^(n^(k+1))` whenever `n ≥ c + 2`, since then
             `c·n^k + c < n·n^k = n^(k+1)`.
Failure analysis : Reusing `pow_pow_succ_gap` verbatim fails because its witness `n = c + 2`
             has a fixed parity, so it can only refute *one* of the two simulations needed
             to sandwich `interPowSys`.  The all-large-`n` form removes that coupling.
-- !-- Lab Notebook -- !--
-/

set_option maxHeartbeats 1000000

namespace ProofComplexity

/-! ## A uniform (all-large-`n`) super-polynomial gap -/

/-
!-- comment: For `k ≥ 1` the rungs `2^(n^k)` and `2^(n^(k+1))` are super-polynomially
apart for *every* `n ≥ c + 2`, not just one — so a witness of either parity
is available. -- !--

**Uniform ladder gap.**  For `k ≥ 1` and every exponent `c`, the inequality
`(2 ^ (n ^ k) + 2) ^ c < 2 ^ (n ^ (k + 1))` holds for *all* `n ≥ c + 2`.
-/
lemma pow_pow_succ_gap_strong (k : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) (c : ℕ) :
    ∀ n, c + 2 ≤ n → (2 ^ (n ^ k) + 2) ^ c < 2 ^ (n ^ (k + 1)) := by
  -- Apply the power inequality: $(2^{n^k} + 2)^c \leq 2^{c \cdot (n^k + 1)}$
  have h_pow : ∀ n, c + 2 ≤ n → (2 ^ (n ^ k) + 2) ^ c ≤ 2 ^ (c * (n ^ k + 1)) := by
    intros n hn; rw [ pow_mul' ] ; gcongr;
    rw [ pow_succ' ] ; linarith [ Nat.pow_le_pow_right ( by decide : 1 ≤ 2 ) ( show n ^ k ≥ 1 by exact Nat.one_le_pow _ _ ( by linarith ) ) ];
  refine fun n hn ↦ lt_of_le_of_lt ( h_pow n hn ) ?_;
  gcongr <;> norm_num;
  rw [ pow_succ' ] ; nlinarith [ Nat.pow_le_pow_right ( by linarith : 1 ≤ n ) hk ] ;

/-! ## The parity-glued intermediate system -/

-- !-- comment: Upper rate `2^(n^(k+1))` on even indices, lower rate `2^(n^k)` on odd
--             indices: a degree glued from the two rates on the two residue classes. -- !--
/-- The parity-glued intermediate system: size `2 ^ (n ^ (k+1))` on even `n`, size
`2 ^ (n ^ k)` on odd `n`. -/
def interPowSys (k : ℕ) : ProofSystem.{0, 0} ℕ :=
  sysOfSize (fun n => if Even n then 2 ^ (n ^ (k + 1)) else 2 ^ (n ^ k))

/-! ## `powSystem k < interPowSys k` -/

/-
!-- comment: Lower rung simulates the glued system (its size is everywhere `≥ 2^(n^k)`),
but the glued system cannot be simulated by the lower rung because the even
indices keep the faster rate (uniform gap at an even witness). -- !--

The lower ladder rung is strictly below the glued system: `powSystem k < interPowSys k`
for `k ≥ 1`.
-/
theorem powSystem_lt_interPow (k : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) :
    powSystem k < interPowSys k := by
  constructor;
  · convert simulates_sysOfSize_iff _ _ |>.2 ⟨ id, polyMono_id, ?_ ⟩;
    intro n; split_ifs <;> simp_all +decide [ Nat.pow_succ ] ;
    rcases n with ( _ | _ | n ) <;> simp_all +decide [ Nat.pow_succ', Nat.pow_mul ];
    · cases k <;> norm_num at *;
    · exact Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero.mpr ( by positivity );
  · intro h;
    obtain ⟨ f, hf_mono, hf_bound ⟩ := simulates_sysOfSize_iff _ _ |>.1 h;
    obtain ⟨ c, hc ⟩ := hf_mono.2;
    have := pow_pow_succ_gap_strong k hk c ( 2 * ( c + 2 ) ) ( by linarith );
    grind

/-! ## `interPowSys k < powSystem (k+1)` -/

/-
!-- comment: The glued system simulates the upper rung (its size is everywhere
`≤ 2^(n^(k+1))`), but the upper rung cannot be simulated by the glued system
because the odd indices fall back to the slower rate (uniform gap at an odd
witness). -- !--

The glued system is strictly below the upper ladder rung: `interPowSys k < powSystem
(k+1)` for `k ≥ 1`.
-/
theorem interPow_lt_powSystem_succ (k : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) :
    interPowSys k < powSystem (k + 1) := by
  refine' lt_of_le_not_ge _ _;
  · refine' simulates_sysOfSize_iff _ _ |>.2 ⟨ _, polyMono_id, fun n => _ ⟩;
    split_ifs <;> [ exact le_rfl; exact pow_le_pow_right₀ ( by decide ) ( Nat.pow_le_pow_right ( Nat.pos_of_ne_zero ( by aesop ) ) ( by linarith ) ) ];
  · -- Suppose for contradiction that `powSystem (k+1) ≤ interPowSys k`.
    by_contra h_contra
    unfold powSystem interPowSys at h_contra;
    obtain ⟨ f, hf_mono, hf_bound ⟩ := simulates_sysOfSize_iff _ _ |>.1 h_contra;
    -- Choose an ODD witness `n := 2 * (c + 2) + 1`. Then `¬ Even n` (so the if-branch is `2^(n^k)`) and `c + 2 ≤ n`.
    obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ : ∃ c, ∀ m, f m + 1 ≤ (m + 2) ^ c := by
      exact hf_mono.2
    set n := 2 * (c + 2) + 1 with hn_def
    have hn_odd : ¬Even n := by
      grind
    have hn_ge : c + 2 ≤ n := by
      grind;
    have := pow_pow_succ_gap_strong k hk c n hn_ge;
    grind

/-! ## Density at every rung -/

-- !-- comment: Sandwiching the two strict steps: a strictly intermediate degree exists
--             between every pair of consecutive ladder rungs. -- !--
/-- **Density along the ladder.**  For every `k ≥ 1` there is a p-degree strictly between
the consecutive ladder rungs `powSystem k` and `powSystem (k+1)`. -/
theorem exists_strictly_between_powSystem (k : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) :
    ∃ S : ProofSystem.{0, 0} ℕ, powSystem k < S ∧ S < powSystem (k + 1) :=
  ⟨interPowSys k, powSystem_lt_interPow k hk, interPow_lt_powSystem_succ k hk⟩

end ProofComplexity

# Obstruction Monotonicity under Divisibility

## Main Results

- `primitiveResidueSolution_of_dvd`: If `M ∣ N` and there is a primitive
  residue solution mod N, then there is one mod M.
- `no_primitiveResidueSolution_of_dvd`: Contrapositive — an obstruction at
  M propagates to all multiples of M.

## Key Insight

The natural ring homomorphism `ZMod N →+* ZMod M` (for `M ∣ N`) sends
units to units and preserves the polynomial equation. This gives solution
inheritance from `N` to divisors `M`.
-/
import Mathlib
import Speculative.Beal.Defs

open ZMod

/-! ## Solution Inheritance -/

/-
Solutions descend from `N` to any divisor `M`: if `M ∣ N` and
`a^x + b^y = c^z` has unit solutions in `ZMod N`, then it has
unit solutions in `ZMod M`.
-/
theorem primitiveResidueSolution_of_dvd
    {M N x y z : ℕ}
    (hdvd : M ∣ N)
    (hsol : PrimitiveResidueSolution N x y z) :
    PrimitiveResidueSolution M x y z := by
  rcases hsol with ⟨ a, b, c, ha, hb, hc, h ⟩;
  -- Use the ring homomorphism `ZMod.castHom hdvd (ZMod M) : ZMod N →+* ZMod M`.
  set f : ZMod N →+* ZMod M := ZMod.castHom hdvd (ZMod M);
  exact ⟨ f a, f b, f c, ha.map f, hb.map f, hc.map f, by simpa using congr_arg f h ⟩

/-- **Obstruction Monotonicity**: if no primitive residue solution exists
mod M, then none exists mod any multiple of M. One obstructing modulus
annihilates all its multiples. -/
theorem no_primitiveResidueSolution_of_dvd
    {M N x y z : ℕ}
    (hdvd : M ∣ N)
    (hno : ¬ PrimitiveResidueSolution M x y z) :
    ¬ PrimitiveResidueSolution N x y z :=
  fun hsol => hno (primitiveResidueSolution_of_dvd hdvd hsol)

# FUTURE DIRECTIONS — Discrete Hodge ↔ Probability

This cycle established a self-contained Mathlib foundation for the discrete Hodge
program on finite weighted graphs and bridged it to the probability of reversible
random walks (file `Catalog/Bridges/DiscreteHodgeRandomWalk.lean`).

Proved this cycle:
- Dirichlet energy identity `xᵀ L x = ½ Σᵢⱼ wᵢⱼ (xᵢ − xⱼ)²`.
- Positive semidefiniteness of the combinatorial Laplacian `L = D − A`.
- Symmetry of `L`, zero row-sums, and harmonicity of constants.
- Detailed balance / reversibility of `P = D⁻¹A` w.r.t. the degree measure
  (stated *unconditionally* using totality of real division).
- The factorization `L f = D(f − Pf)` and the bridge theorem:
  at a positive-degree vertex, `(L f) i = 0 ⟺ (P f) i = f i`
  (discrete harmonic forms = walk-invariant functions).

The following conjectures are bold, precise, and testable in subsequent cycles.

## C1 — Kernel of `L` = locally constant functions (connectivity ⇒ 0th Hodge number)
For a finite weighted graph whose positive-weight relation is connected,
`L.mulVec f = 0 ↔ f` is constant. More generally, `dim ker L` equals the number
of connected components of the support graph. This is the discrete `H⁰` and the
0th Betti number; it is the natural next theorem after `laplacian_mulVec_const`
and `quadForm_nonneg` (the energy `½ Σ wᵢⱼ(fᵢ−fⱼ)²` vanishes iff `f` is constant
on each component).

## C2 — Spectral gap ⇒ exponential mixing of the reversible walk
Let `0 = λ₀ ≤ λ₁ ≤ … ` be the eigenvalues of the *normalized* Laplacian
`𝓛 = I − D^{-1/2} A D^{-1/2}`. Conjecture: for a connected graph with
`λ₁ > 0`, the reversible walk `P` satisfies a Poincaré inequality
`Var_π(f) ≤ (1/λ₁) · 𝓔(f, f)` (Dirichlet form), hence `Lᵖ` mixing
`‖Pᵗf − π(f)‖ ≤ (1 − λ₁)ᵗ ‖f‖`. This connects the Hodge spectrum directly to
the probabilistic convergence rate; the Dirichlet identity proved here is the
exact `𝓔(f,f)` appearing in the inequality.

## C3 — Discrete Hodge decomposition `ℝ^V = ker L ⊕ im L`
Because `L` is symmetric PSD, `ℝ^V` orthogonally decomposes as
`ker L ⊕ range L`, with `ker L` the harmonic part and `range L` the "exact +
co-exact" part. Conjecture (and formalize): every function uniquely splits as
`f = h + Lg` with `h` harmonic, and `h` is the orthogonal projection minimizing
Dirichlet energy among representatives of `f mod range L`. This is the finite-
dimensional Hodge theorem; it needs only `Matrix.IsSymm` + PSD already proved.

## C4 — Reversibility characterizes self-adjointness of `P` in the `π`-inner product
Conjecture: a stochastic kernel `P` on `Fin n` is reversible w.r.t. a positive
measure `π` (`πᵢ Pᵢⱼ = πⱼ Pⱼᵢ`) **iff** `P` is self-adjoint for the weighted
inner product `⟨f,g⟩_π = Σ πᵢ fᵢ gᵢ`, **iff** `P` arises from some symmetric
weight kernel `w` via `wᵢⱼ = πᵢ Pᵢⱼ`. This upgrades `reversible` from a property
of graph-derived walks to a full equivalence, identifying "reversible Markov
chain" with "weighted graph" canonically.

## C5 — Effective resistance is a metric, and a graph-Green's-function identity
Define effective resistance `R(i,j)` via the energy-minimizing `g` with
`L g = eᵢ − eⱼ` (well-defined on connected graphs by C3). Conjecture:
`R` is a metric on vertices (the "resistance metric"), `R(i,j) = (eᵢ−eⱼ)ᵀ L⁺ (eᵢ−eⱼ)`
with `L⁺` the Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse, and it equals the expected commute
time of the reversible walk up to the factor `2·(total weight)`. This is the
deepest probability↔Hodge bridge: the Green's function `L⁺` simultaneously
governs harmonic extension (Hodge) and commute/hitting times (probability).

open Classical
open Bridges.AlgebraMachineLearning
open Bridges.NeuralProofSpectrum

namespace Bridges.NeuralProofSpectrumDeep

universe u v w

variable {R S K : Type*} {α : Type*}

/-! ## Section 0: the underlying coalgebra and depth-wise agreement

We abbreviate the underlying (unweighted) neural observation system and recall the
definitional identity `neural_behavior (toNeural N) = algBehavior N`.
-/

/-- The underlying coalgebra of an algebraic neural system. -/
def toNeural [Semiring R] [Semiring K] (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) :
    NeuralObservationSystem R α K :=
  weighted_to_neural N.toWeighted

theorem neural_behavior_eq_algBehavior [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) (x : R) (w : List α) :
    neural_behavior (toNeural N) x w = algBehavior N x w := rfl

/-- Depth-`k` agreement of two states (agree on all contexts of length `≤ k`). -/
def agreeUpto [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) (k : ℕ) (x y : R) : Prop :=
  neural_equiv_upto (toNeural N) k x y

theorem agreeUpto_iff [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) (k : ℕ) (x y : R) :
    agreeUpto N k x y ↔ ∀ w : List α, w.length ≤ k → algBehavior N x w = algBehavior N y w :=
  Iff.rfl

theorem agreeUpto_symm [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) {k : ℕ} {x y : R}
    (h : agreeUpto N k x y) : agreeUpto N k y x :=
  fun w hw => (h w hw).symm

theorem agreeUpto_trans [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) {k : ℕ} {x y z : R}
    (hxy : agreeUpto N k x y) (hyz : agreeUpto N k y z) : agreeUpto N k x z :=
  fun w hw => (hxy w hw).trans (hyz w hw)

theorem agreeUpto_mono [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) {j k : ℕ} (hjk : j ≤ k) {x y : R}
    (h : agreeUpto N k x y) : agreeUpto N j x y :=
  fun w hw => h w (hw.trans hjk)

/-- Behavioral equivalence is exactly agreement at every depth. -/
theorem behaviorRel_iff_agree_all [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) (x y : R) :
    behaviorRel N x y ↔ ∀ k, agreeUpto N k x y :=
  behaviorRel_iff_all_depth N x y

/-! ## Section 1: separating depth and the graded ultrametric

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
-- Hypothesis H1 (resolving F1).  Define `sepDepth x y = sInf {k | ¬ agreeUpto N k x y}`.
-- When `x ≁ y` the set is nonempty (a separating word of some length exists), so
-- `sepDepth` is a genuine least separating depth and lands *in* the set
-- (`Nat.sInf_mem`).  Guarded by `if behaviorRel` the distance `2^(-sepDepth)` is well
-- defined and strictly positive off the diagonal.
--
-- Insight I1.  The STRONG triangle inequality holds.  Key combinatorial fact:
-- depth-`m` agreement is, for each fixed `m`, an equivalence relation (`agreeUpto_trans`).
-- If `x ≁ z` and `m = sepDepth x z`, then if BOTH `gradedDist x y < gradedDist x z` and
-- `gradedDist y z < gradedDist x z`, we would get `agreeUpto m x y` and `agreeUpto m y z`,
-- hence `agreeUpto m x z` — contradicting `m ∈ {k | ¬ agreeUpto N k x z}`.  Hence the max
-- of the two dominates, which is exactly the ultrametric inequality.
-/

/-- The least observation depth that separates `x` from `y` (`0` by convention when they
    are behaviorally equivalent — guarded away in `gradedDist`). -/
def sepDepth [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) (x y : R) : ℕ :=
  sInf {k | ¬ agreeUpto N k x y}

theorem sepDepth_symm [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) (x y : R) :
    sepDepth N x y = sepDepth N y x := by
  unfold sepDepth
  congr 1
  ext k
  exact ⟨fun h hh => h (agreeUpto_symm N hh), fun h hh => h (agreeUpto_symm N hh)⟩

/-- If `x ≁ y` the separating set is nonempty, so `sepDepth` realises an actual
    separating depth: `x` and `y` do **not** agree up to `sepDepth N x y`. -/
theorem not_agree_sepDepth [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) {x y : R} (h : ¬ behaviorRel N x y) :
    ¬ agreeUpto N (sepDepth N x y) x y := by
  have hne : {k | ¬ agreeUpto N k x y}.Nonempty := by
    by_contra hc
    apply h
    rw [behaviorRel_iff_agree_all]
    intro k
    by_contra hk
    exact hc ⟨k, hk⟩
  exact Nat.sInf_mem hne

/-- If a depth `j` is below the separating depth, the states agree up to `j`. -/
theorem agree_of_lt_sepDepth [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) {x y : R} {j : ℕ} (hj : j < sepDepth N x y) :
    agreeUpto N j x y := by
  by_contra hc
  have : sepDepth N x y ≤ j := Nat.sInf_le hc
  omega

/-- The **depth-graded observation ultrametric**: distance `0` for behaviorally
    indistinguishable states, else `2^(-d)` where `d` is the least separating depth. -/
def gradedDist [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) (x y : R) : ℝ :=
  if behaviorRel N x y then 0 else (2 : ℝ) ^ (-(sepDepth N x y : ℤ))

theorem gradedDist_nonneg [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) (x y : R) : 0 ≤ gradedDist N x y := by
  unfold gradedDist
  split_ifs with h
  · exact le_refl 0
  · positivity

theorem gradedDist_self [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) (x : R) : gradedDist N x x = 0 := by
  simp [gradedDist, behaviorRel_refl]

theorem gradedDist_comm [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) (x y : R) : gradedDist N x y = gradedDist N y x := by
  unfold gradedDist
  rw [sepDepth_symm N x y]
  by_cases h : behaviorRel N x y
  · rw [if_pos h, if_pos (behaviorRel_symm N h)]
  · rw [if_neg h, if_neg (fun hh => h (behaviorRel_symm N hh))]

theorem gradedDist_eq_zero_iff [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) (x y : R) :
    gradedDist N x y = 0 ↔ behaviorRel N x y := by
  unfold gradedDist
  split_ifs with h
  · simp [h]
  · constructor
    · intro hz
      exact absurd hz (by positivity)
    · intro hh; exact absurd hh h

/-- Positivity off the diagonal, with the explicit value. -/
theorem gradedDist_of_not_rel [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) {x y : R} (h : ¬ behaviorRel N x y) :
    gradedDist N x y = (2 : ℝ) ^ (-(sepDepth N x y : ℤ)) := by
  simp [gradedDist, h]

/-- The graded ultrametric **refines** the discrete observation pseudometric:
    `gradedDist ≤ obsDist` everywhere (and they share the same kernel). -/
theorem gradedDist_le_obsDist [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) (x y : R) :
    gradedDist N x y ≤ obsDist N x y := by
  unfold gradedDist obsDist
  split_ifs with h
  · norm_num
  · have : (2 : ℝ) ^ (-(sepDepth N x y : ℤ)) ≤ 1 := by
      apply zpow_le_one_of_nonpos₀ (by norm_num)
      simp
    simpa using this

/-- The kernel of the graded ultrametric is exactly the proof-spectrum congruence. -/
theorem gradedDist_kernel_eq_congruence [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) (x y : R) :
    gradedDist N x y = 0 ↔ (behaviorCongruence N).rel x y := by
  rw [gradedDist_eq_zero_iff]; rfl

/-! ### The ultrametric (strong triangle) inequality

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
-- Result R1 (resolving F1).  The crux is `gradedDist_strong_triangle`.  The helper
-- `agree_of_dist_lt` says: if `gradedDist x y < gradedDist x z` (with `x ≁ z`), then `x`
-- and `y` agree up to `m = sepDepth x z`.  Two regimes: if `x ~ y` it is automatic; else
-- `2^(-sepDepth x y) < 2^(-m)` forces `sepDepth x y > m`, hence `agreeUpto m x y` by
-- `agree_of_lt_sepDepth`.  Combining the two helpers with `agreeUpto_trans` against
-- `not_agree_sepDepth` gives the contradiction, i.e. the strong triangle bound.
-/

/-- If a state `y` is strictly closer to `x` than `z` is, then `x` and `y` agree up to the
    separating depth of `x` and `z`. -/
theorem agree_of_dist_lt [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) {x y z : R} (hxz : ¬ behaviorRel N x z)
    (hlt : gradedDist N x y < gradedDist N x z) :
    agreeUpto N (sepDepth N x z) x y := by
  by_cases hxy : behaviorRel N x y
  · -- behavioral equivalence implies agreement at every depth
    exact (behaviorRel_iff_agree_all N x y).mp hxy _
  · -- strict inequality on the exponentials forces a deeper separation depth
    rw [gradedDist_of_not_rel N hxy, gradedDist_of_not_rel N hxz] at hlt
    have hbase : (1 : ℝ) < 2 := by norm_num
    have hexp : (-(sepDepth N x y : ℤ)) < (-(sepDepth N x z : ℤ)) :=
      (zpow_lt_zpow_iff_right₀ hbase).mp hlt
    have : (sepDepth N x z : ℤ) < (sepDepth N x y : ℤ) := by omega
    have hmlt : sepDepth N x z < sepDepth N x y := by exact_mod_cast this
    exact agree_of_lt_sepDepth N hmlt

/-- **The ultrametric inequality.** `gradedDist` satisfies the strong triangle
    inequality, so the observation distance is a genuine pseudo-ultrametric. -/
theorem gradedDist_strong_triangle [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) (x y z : R) :
    gradedDist N x z ≤ max (gradedDist N x y) (gradedDist N y z) := by
  by_cases hxz : behaviorRel N x z
  · rw [(gradedDist_eq_zero_iff N x z).mpr hxz]
    exact le_max_of_le_left (gradedDist_nonneg N x y)
  · -- it suffices that not both legs are strictly shorter than `x`–`z`
    rw [le_max_iff]
    by_contra hcon
    push_neg at hcon
    obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := hcon
    have hxy : agreeUpto N (sepDepth N x z) x y := agree_of_dist_lt N hxz h1
    have hyz : agreeUpto N (sepDepth N x z) y z := by
      have hzx : ¬ behaviorRel N z x := fun h => hxz (behaviorRel_symm N h)
      have hlt : gradedDist N z y < gradedDist N z x := by
        rw [gradedDist_comm N z y, gradedDist_comm N z x]; exact h2
      have hzy := agree_of_dist_lt N hzx hlt
      rw [sepDepth_symm N z x] at hzy
      exact agreeUpto_symm N hzy
    exact not_agree_sepDepth N hxz (agreeUpto_trans N hxy hyz)

/-! ## Section 2: functoriality is non-expansive (Lipschitz geometry)

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
-- Result R2 (geometric functoriality).  In the base file morphisms preserve the kernel.
-- Here we sharpen this to a *metric* statement: an `AlgNeuralHom` is non-expansive for the
-- graded ultrametric.  Reason: depth-`k` agreement is preserved by morphisms (immediate
-- from `algBehavior_map`), so the separating set of the image is contained in that of the
-- source, whence `sepDepth` can only grow, whence the distance can only shrink.
-/

/-- Morphisms preserve depth-wise agreement (they can only merge states). -/
theorem agreeUpto_map [Semiring R] [Semiring S] [Semiring K]
    {N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α} {M : AlgNeuralSystem S K α} (f : AlgNeuralHom N M)
    {k : ℕ} {x y : R} (h : agreeUpto N k x y) :
    agreeUpto M k (f.toFun x) (f.toFun y) := by
  intro w hw
  rw [neural_behavior_eq_algBehavior, neural_behavior_eq_algBehavior,
      ← algBehavior_map f x w, ← algBehavior_map f y w]
  exact h w hw

/-- Morphisms cannot decrease the separating depth. -/
theorem sepDepth_map_ge [Semiring R] [Semiring S] [Semiring K]
    {N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α} {M : AlgNeuralSystem S K α} (f : AlgNeuralHom N M)
    {x y : R} (h : ¬ behaviorRel M (f.toFun x) (f.toFun y)) :
    sepDepth N x y ≤ sepDepth M (f.toFun x) (f.toFun y) := by
  -- the image separates at `sepDepth M`, hence so does the source
  have hsep : ¬ agreeUpto N (sepDepth M (f.toFun x) (f.toFun y)) x y := by
    intro hc
    exact not_agree_sepDepth M h (agreeUpto_map f hc)
  exact Nat.sInf_le hsep

/-- **Non-expansiveness.** An `AlgNeuralHom` is `1`-Lipschitz for the graded ultrametric:
    images are never farther apart than their preimages. -/
theorem gradedDist_map_le [Semiring R] [Semiring S] [Semiring K]
    {N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α} {M : AlgNeuralSystem S K α} (f : AlgNeuralHom N M)
    (x y : R) :
    gradedDist M (f.toFun x) (f.toFun y) ≤ gradedDist N x y := by
  by_cases hM : behaviorRel M (f.toFun x) (f.toFun y)
  · rw [(gradedDist_eq_zero_iff M (f.toFun x) (f.toFun y)).mpr hM]
    exact gradedDist_nonneg N x y
  · have hN : ¬ behaviorRel N x y := by
      intro h
      exact hM (behaviorCongruence_map f h)
    rw [gradedDist_of_not_rel M hM, gradedDist_of_not_rel N hN]
    have hge : sepDepth N x y ≤ sepDepth M (f.toFun x) (f.toFun y) := sepDepth_map_ge f hM
    have hexp : (-(sepDepth M (f.toFun x) (f.toFun y) : ℤ)) ≤ -(sepDepth N x y : ℤ) := by
      simp only [neg_le_neg_iff]; exact_mod_cast hge
    exact zpow_le_zpow_right₀ (by norm_num) hexp

/-! ## Section 3: a primality criterion (resolving F2)

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
-- Hypothesis H2 (resolving F2).  The base file noted that primality of
-- `behaviorCongruence N` fails because the pointwise factorisation
-- `∀ w, b(a,w)=0 ∨ b(b,w)=0` does not pull out the quantifier.  The clean cure is a
-- *faithful observation point*: a single context `w₀` whose vanishing already detects
-- behavioral nullity, `behaviorRel N a 0 ↔ algBehavior N a w₀ = 0`.  Then in an integral
-- domain `K`, `algBehavior N (a*b) w₀ = algBehavior N a w₀ * algBehavior N b w₀ = 0`
-- factors at the single point `w₀`, and faithfulness lifts each branch back to behavioral
-- nullity.  This yields a genuine `PrimeSRCong R` — an honest point of `ProofSpectrum R`.
--
-- Failure analysis F3.  Faithfulness is a real restriction (it forces a "generic
-- point").  Without it, primality can fail even over a field; the conjecture in
-- FUTURE_DIRECTIONS.md asks for the exact class of systems admitting a faithful point.
-/

/-- A **faithful observation point**: a context `w₀` whose vanishing detects behavioral
    nullity (`a` is behaviorally null iff its `w₀`-observation is `0`). -/
def FaithfulPoint [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) (w₀ : List α) : Prop :=
  ∀ a : R, behaviorRel N a 0 ↔ algBehavior N a w₀ = 0

/-- **Primality criterion.** With a faithful observation point and an integral-domain
    output, the behavior congruence is prime. -/
theorem behaviorRel_prime_of_faithful [Semiring R] [Semiring K] [IsDomain K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) {w₀ : List α} (hf : FaithfulPoint N w₀)
    {a b : R} (h : behaviorRel N (a * b) 0) :
    behaviorRel N a 0 ∨ behaviorRel N b 0 := by
  have hab : algBehavior N (a * b) w₀ = 0 := (hf (a * b)).mp h
  rw [algBehavior_mul] at hab
  rcases mul_eq_zero.mp hab with ha | hb
  · exact Or.inl ((hf a).mpr ha)
  · exact Or.inr ((hf b).mpr hb)

/-- **The prime functor object.** Under a faithful point and an integral-domain output,
    the behavior congruence upgrades to a `PrimeSRCong R` — a point of the proof
    spectrum. -/
def behaviorPrimeCongruence [Semiring R] [Semiring K] [IsDomain K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) {w₀ : List α} (hf : FaithfulPoint N w₀) :
    PrimeSRCong R where
  toSRCong := behaviorCongruence N
  prime_prop := fun h => behaviorRel_prime_of_faithful N hf h

/-- The prime behavior congruence is, in particular, a point of the `ProofSpectrum`. -/
def behaviorPrimeCongruence_mem_spectrum [Semiring R] [Semiring K] [IsDomain K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) {w₀ : List α} (hf : FaithfulPoint N w₀) :
    ProofSpectrum R :=
  behaviorPrimeCongruence N hf

/-- The vanishing locus of the proof-spectrum point is exactly the behaviorally-null
    states, detected by the faithful point `w₀`. -/
theorem behaviorPrime_vanishes_iff [Semiring R] [Semiring K] [IsDomain K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) {w₀ : List α} (hf : FaithfulPoint N w₀) (a : R) :
    vanishes (behaviorPrimeCongruence_mem_spectrum N hf) a ↔ algBehavior N a w₀ = 0 := by
  exact hf a

/-! ## Section 4: capstone — the deepened comparison

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
-- Summary S1.  Bundling the deepened facts: the graded ultrametric, the discrete
-- pseudometric, the coalgebraic behavioral equivalence, and the proof-spectrum congruence
-- all share one kernel; and the graded distance dominates none of them — it refines the
-- discrete pseudometric while carrying strictly more information (the separating depth).
-/

/-- The deepened comparison: graded ultrametric kernel, discrete pseudometric kernel,
    coalgebraic behavioral equivalence, and proof-spectrum congruence all coincide, and
    the graded ultrametric refines the discrete pseudometric. -/
theorem deep_neural_pseudometric_comparison [Semiring R] [Semiring K]
    (N : AlgNeuralSystem R K α) (x y : R) :
    (gradedDist N x y = 0 ↔ obsDist N x y = 0) ∧
    (obsDist N x y = 0 ↔ (behaviorCongruence N).rel x y) ∧
    gradedDist N x y ≤ obsDist N x y := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, gradedDist_le_obsDist N x y⟩
  · rw [gradedDist_eq_zero_iff, obsDist_eq_zero_iff]
  · rw [obsDist_eq_zero_iff]; rfl

end Bridges.NeuralProofSpectrumDeep

# Obstruction Monotonicity under Divisibility

## Main Results

- `primitiveResidueSolution_of_dvd`: If `M ∣ N` and there is a primitive
  residue solution mod N, then there is one mod M.
- `no_primitiveResidueSolution_of_dvd`: Contrapositive — an obstruction at
  M propagates to all multiples of M.

## Key Insight

The natural ring homomorphism `ZMod N →+* ZMod M` (for `M ∣ N`) sends
units to units and preserves the polynomial equation. This gives solution
inheritance from `N` to divisors `M`.
-/
import Mathlib
import Speculative.Beal.Defs

open ZMod

/-! ## Solution Inheritance -/

/-
Solutions descend from `N` to any divisor `M`: if `M ∣ N` and
`a^x + b^y = c^z` has unit solutions in `ZMod N`, then it has
unit solutions in `ZMod M`.
-/
theorem primitiveResidueSolution_of_dvd
    {M N x y z : ℕ}
    (hdvd : M ∣ N)
    (hsol : PrimitiveResidueSolution N x y z) :
    PrimitiveResidueSolution M x y z := by
  rcases hsol with ⟨ a, b, c, ha, hb, hc, h ⟩;
  -- Use the ring homomorphism `ZMod.castHom hdvd (ZMod M) : ZMod N →+* ZMod M`.
  set f : ZMod N →+* ZMod M := ZMod.castHom hdvd (ZMod M);
  exact ⟨ f a, f b, f c, ha.map f, hb.map f, hc.map f, by simpa using congr_arg f h ⟩

/-- **Obstruction Monotonicity**: if no primitive residue solution exists
mod M, then none exists mod any multiple of M. One obstructing modulus
annihilates all its multiples. -/
theorem no_primitiveResidueSolution_of_dvd
    {M N x y z : ℕ}
    (hdvd : M ∣ N)
    (hno : ¬ PrimitiveResidueSolution M x y z) :
    ¬ PrimitiveResidueSolution N x y z :=
  fun hsol => hno (primitiveResidueSolution_of_dvd hdvd hsol)
